source.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Evaluating Embedding Model Similarity for Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
source.authors: Laura Caspari; Kanishka Ghosh Dastidar; S. Zerhoudi; Jelena Mitrović; Michael Granitzer

record.tranche_reason: The study measures embedding and retrieval similarity with multiple metrics and datasets, and finds that similarity is incomplete and depends on the metric, retrieval cutoff, and dataset. It refines similarity claims rather than testing convergence with scale.
record.gate_note: The study compares 19 text embedding models using CKA and retrieval-similarity measures. Its MTEB scores are model-description/selection information; it does not analyze whether similarity rises with model size or capability. The extensive pairwise matrices and curves are not fully transcribed here. No vision-language, seed, feature-recurrence, or representation-mapping tests are reported.
record.test_reason: The study compares 19 independently trained text embedding models from different families. It uses linear CKA and two retrieval-overlap measures (Jaccard and rank similarity) across five BEIR datasets and many top-k cutoffs. Its own numbers show that apparent similarity depends on the measure, k and dataset (V6), and that agreement is mostly far from complete (V7). It does not relate similarity to scale or capability (V1).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. CKA shows intra- and inter-family clusters, which reappear in retrieval similarity only at large k. At the small k used in RAG, retrieval similarity varies widely and is much lower, especially on larger datasets. Choosing a model therefore remains non-trivial.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear CKA for embedding comparisons and adds Jaccard and rank similarity for retrieval outputs; it does not reproduce a scale-convergence experiment from the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Similarity patterns vary with metric, k, and dataset; the authors report particularly high variance at small k and lower retrieval similarity on larger datasets.
record.problems: Only five comparatively small BEIR datasets were used; retrieval similarity is averaged over 25 queries. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The authors note that the datasets are small compared with real-world RAG corpora and that only a small sample of similarity measures was evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: The full pairwise CKA matrix and the detailed pairwise retrieval-similarity matrices/curves contain many additional model-pair values. These are not transcribed individually; see Figures 1-6. The text also summarizes additional dataset-specific rankings without giving a single aggregate value.

untested.parts: Similarity is never related to model size or MTEB capability. The authors list this as future work.
No runs of the same architecture from different seeds.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests.
No analysis of features, neurons or circuits.
Only linear CKA, Jaccard and rank similarity are used. There are no kernel or neighbour-count settings of a representational measure, and no out-of-distribution inputs.
No plateau-with-scale analysis. No causal test of whether shared data, objectives or lineage explain the family and inter-family clusters.

missing.what: Top-10 rank-similarity matrix on NFCorpus; its clusters differ from the Jaccard clusters (further metric dependence)
Top-10 Jaccard matrices for SciFact and ArguAna (e.g. UAE–mxbai 0.76 and 0.89; most other pairs about 0.2–0.5)
Cross-family CKA between the top MTEB models (Mistral–OpenAI 0.84–0.87; Cohere–e5-large 0.93) next to low retrieval overlap; usable as an unanalysed capability-related data point

record.verdict_notes: The models are text-only embedding models that differ in architecture, training and data. The study is not one of the original sources. Because size and capability are never analysed, V1 cannot be judged. The record's V7 'supports' label wrongly cited r2–r4; those rows show near-complete alignment and are relabelled limits_scope. Retrieval overlap is a functional measure, so V6 support here means representational and functional measures disagree, rather than settings of one representational metric.

versions.untested_parts: No analysis of similarity increasing with model size or capability; the models' MTEB scores and sizes are not related to similarity trends.
No paired image-caption or cross-modal models.
No independently initialized runs of the same architecture or shared-subspace/feature comparison.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No interpretable feature, neuron, SAE-feature, or circuit recurrence analysis.
Tests CKA, Jaccard and rank similarity across selected BEIR datasets and retrieval cutoffs; does not test out-of-distribution inputs or a broad range of metric settings beyond those described.

Reports incomplete retrieval overlap and varying representational similarity, but does not test whether similarity plateaus with scale or whether shared training data/objectives rather than a common model of reality cause it.

rows.subject: 19 embedding models (pairwise comparisons)
rows.operation_detail: Mean pairwise linear CKA across five BEIR datasets
rows.value: High similarity across most models, with identifiable within-family and inter-family clusters; some inter-family scores are highest.
rows.note: The text describes the overall pattern; it does not report one aggregate numerical CKA value for all pairs.
rows.check: Mean CKA values in Figure 1 span about 0.61–0.99, so alignment is incomplete for most pairs. For V6 this row is the high-CKA side of the contrast with r7–r12; on its own it shows no metric dependence.

source_check.correct: For V6, this CKA-only measurement cannot determine metric dependence without comparison to other rows. For V7, incompleteness is observed for most pairs, with near-perfect exceptions.
source_check.problem: One partial state obscures the different implications for V6 and V7.

rows.subject: bge-large-en-v1.5 vs UAE-Large-V1
rows.operation_detail: Pairwise embedding similarity using linear CKA
rows.note: Pairwise value read from the labeled CKA matrix; the paper characterizes this inter-family cluster as almost perfectly similar.
rows.check: Near-perfect CKA (0.99) means the incompleteness V7 predicts is absent for this pair, so it is not 'observed'. The paper notes these models share embedding dimension, size and similar MTEB scores. Shared lineage is plausible but untested.

rows.subject: gte-large compared with other models
rows.operation_detail: Jaccard similarity of retrieved chunks over varying k
rows.value: Scores peak and vary substantially at very small k, drop noticeably, and converge to one for larger k.
rows.note: The authors state that small-k results can differ from the model clusters seen at larger k.
rows.check: Shows Jaccard similarity and cluster membership varying with k. The CKA clusters only reappear at large k. This bears on V6, not on how complete alignment is (V7).

rows.subject: gte-large compared with other models
rows.operation_detail: Rank similarity of retrieved chunks over varying k
rows.value: Scores peak at small k, then drop quickly and approach a low stable score for larger k; mxbai, rather than another gte model, has the highest rank similarity to gte-large.
rows.note: The text describes low rank similarity at larger k and variation in which model is most similar.
rows.check: Rank-similarity clusters differ from CKA clusters (mxbai, not a gte model, is closest to gte-large), which is metric dependence. Rank similarity is low at large k, so V7 is observed too.

source_check.locator_found: Figure 2 caption; Section 5.1 rank-similarity paragraph, lines 743–754.

rows.subject: 19 embedding models (pairwise top-10 retrieval comparisons)
rows.operation_detail: Jaccard similarity of top-10 retrieved chunks, averaged over 25 queries
rows.value: Even the most similar models score above 0.6, while the majority of pairwise scores are below 0.5.
rows.note: The study contrasts low top-10 overlap with higher representational similarity.
rows.check: The paper's wording 'even the most similar... higher than 0.6' is odd; the NFCorpus top-10 Jaccard maximum in Figure 4a is 0.74 (UAE–mxbai). Most pairs are below 0.5 despite CKA of about 0.7–0.9. This is clear evidence for both versions, not partial.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, lines 755–765; Figure 4(a), lines 786–804; caption at line 871.

rows.subject: 19 embedding models (pairwise top-10 retrieval comparisons)
rows.operation_detail: Jaccard similarity of top-10 retrieved chunks, averaged over 25 queries
rows.value: Scores are generally substantially lower than on the smaller datasets; most models retrieve almost completely distinct chunks, with the bge/UAE/mxbai cluster retaining notable similarity.
rows.note: The paper reports lower retrieval similarity for this larger dataset.
rows.check: FiQA top-10 Jaccard is mostly about 0.05–0.3, lower than on the smaller datasets. The full effect is present.

rows.subject: Cohere embed-english-v3.0 compared with other models
rows.operation_detail: Jaccard similarity of top-10 retrieved chunks
rows.value: The highest score across datasets is 0.51 on ArguAna; the most similar model varies by dataset.
rows.note: The study explicitly reports dataset-dependent variation and no consistently most similar model for Cohere.

rows.subject: SFR-Embedding-Mistral vs OpenAI text-embedding-3 models
rows.value: For text-embedding-3-large, the highest score on smaller datasets is about 0.6; on TREC-COVID it is 0.18. Text-embedding-3-small scores are described as close to those of other models across datasets.
rows.note: The authors state that Mistral is largely the most similar model to OpenAI at top 10, but absolute retrieval similarity is low to moderate and varies by dataset.
rows.check: Top-10 Jaccard falls from about 0.6 on the smaller datasets to 0.18 on TREC-COVID, so it depends on the dataset.

relationships.condition: 19 text embedding models, five BEIR datasets; CKA versus top-k Jaccard and rank similarity
relationships.reason: Similarity is high under CKA but low under top-10 retrieval overlap. Clusters shift with k and with the measure, and overlap drops on the larger datasets (r1, r5–r12).
relationships.display_finding: CKA indicated high similarity despite low top-10 retrieval overlap; model clusters changed with k and metric, and overlap decreased on larger datasets.

relation.reason: The study directly measures representational and retrieval similarity across models and datasets.

tranche.reason: Its own comparisons show that similarity depends on measure, retrieval cutoff and dataset, qualifying broad interpretations of convergence.

source_check.notes: CKA and retrieval overlap measure different observables; their scores do not share a completeness threshold. Independent training histories, common origin, causal explanations and convergence plateaus are not established by this study.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Compared measures, retrieval cutoffs, and the five tested BEIR datasets
reader_labels.reason: Similarity patterns and scores change with metric and k, and retrieval similarity is generally lower on the larger datasets (r1, r5-r12).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Top-10 retrieval comparisons, especially on FiQA-2018 and TREC-COVID
reader_labels.reason: Top-10 retrieval overlap is limited for most pairs and can be very low on the larger datasets, while the strong CKA cluster does not guarantee comparable retrieved chunks (r2-r4, r7-r10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Embedding-space CKA compared with retrieval similarity across tested models
reader_labels.reason: CKA shows high and sometimes near-perfect pairwise similarity, but that alignment does not reliably transfer to top-k retrieval overlap (r1-r4, r7-r10).
